title: ADAS — Unit economics
description: What a unit of AI work costs: per turn, per conversation, per resolved conversation, and per client. Answers 'is the gateway paying off' rather than 'what did we spend'. Served by ADAS (POST /v1/queries/execute-sql) — never by a direct ClickHouse datasource; ReplacingMergeTree deduplication (FINAL) is applied server-side.

panels.title: Read this before trusting a number

options.content:
**Read the denominators, not just the dollars.** Total spend answers nothing on its own; cost per unit of delivered work does.

**Read cost by outcome.** Compare what a *partially resolved* conversation costs with a *resolved* and an *unresolved* one: when the partly solved ones are the dearest, users are pushing on, cost accrues and the outcome stays half-finished. The ratio moves with the traffic mix — read it off the outcome table, not off this note.

**Two spines, deliberately.** Per-turn and per-client figures come from the usage log using `deployment_price`. Per-conversation figures come from the `conversations` rollup using its own `total_price` (which sums per-hop costs, so it does not double-count). The two do not add together — conversations cover chat traffic only, since native harness traffic carries no chat id.

**Outcome labels can cover only part of the population.** Only conversations `conversation_insights` has labelled carry a `resolution_status` — whenever it lags or stalls, `unlabelled` dominates both conversations and spend, and many labelled rows can be `truncated` (computed from part of the conversation because it exceeded the assembly caps). A large share of conversations can carry no `total_price` at all (unpriced deployments, negligible tokens) and count as $0 in every per-conversation average. Treat outcome mix as indicative, not exact.

**Client attribution is complete.** Once identity enrichment has backfilled to the oldest usage-log row, the per-client panel keeps its 'unattributed' bucket as a safety net, and it stays empty. What is partial is *pricing*: a large share of hops, chat and Claude Code included, can carry no `deployment_price`, so per-client dollars are a floor.

**Served by ADAS, never by a direct ClickHouse datasource.** Every panel on this dashboard goes through `POST /v1/queries/execute-sql`, so it runs inside the governed pipeline: entity and field validation, a closed function catalog, per-column visibility, and a hard **1,000-row cap** per result. **Deduplication is the service's job** — `FINAL` is applied server-side, so there is no raw-read inflation to guard against here. **`deployment_price`, not `total_price`** for usage-log cost: it is a hop's own cost, so summing it over hops does not double-count a routed chain.

**Four properties of ADAS's SQL surface shape every panel's SQL** (the dialect in full: `docs/sql-reference.md`). (1) There are no `$__timeFilter` / `$__timeInterval` macros — the range is interpolated as `TIMESTAMP` literals from Grafana's own `__from` / `__to` globals via their `:date:` formatter, and buckets are fixed-width `date_bin(n, unit, col)`, so **bucket width does not follow panel width**. (2) Enrichment tables are never joined — they are read as dotted columns on the spine (`usage_client_identity.client_type`, `session_insights.activity`), which never drops a spine row: in a plain single-entity statement like every query here, a missing enrichment row reads the column's type default (`''` for a non-nullable string), not NULL — NULL is what an unmatched side yields inside an explicit join, and these panels use none, which is why coverage is tested with `<> ''`. (3) an `enum` column can be *compared* with a string literal directly (`= 'x'`, `<> 'x'`, `IN (…)`), but cannot be *produced* alongside one — `coalesce(enum, 'none')` or a `CASE` returning either is rejected once the result is grouped, so those go through `to_string()` first. (4) `countIf` / `uniqExactIf` / `multiIf` / `quantile` have no direct equivalent; they are `count(CASE WHEN ...)`, `count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN ...)`, `CASE WHEN`, and `percentile_cont(p) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY col)` — which renders to the same ClickHouse `quantile()` — a reservoir estimate on both sides, so p95 values match the original exactly while both can sit a few percent off the exact percentile on groups above ~8k values.

**Panel choices worth knowing.** The `—` placeholder in *Cost by kind of work* is an ASCII `-`: a non-Latin-1 string literal is currently rejected with HTTP 500. *Cost per turn over time* buckets **daily** (the original was hourly): unweighted hourly ratios can be dominated by low-volume hours and read well above the window-wide cost per turn shown in the headline row. *Prompt cache hit rate over time* plots the rate over cache-reporting traffic as well as over all prompt tokens, because a large share of calls (embeddings, toolsets, several apps) report no cache field at all and dilute the all-token rate.

panels.title: Cost per unit of work
panels.description: Cost per unit of delivered work over the dashboard window, on the usage-log spine with server-side deduplication. 'Dollar per turn' divides all spend by distinct trace_ids (one trace = one interaction, including its deployment-to-deployment fan-out). 'Dollar per conversation' divides only chat-attributed spend (rows with a non-empty chat_id) by the distinct chat_ids in that spend, so it is comparable with the conversations-rollup panels below (the two should agree closely). 'Chat share of spend' says how much of the spend that chat denominator covers: the rest is native-harness traffic that carries no chat id. 'Dollar per Mtok' uses total_tokens (prompt + completion). 'Prompt cache hit' is token-weighted: sum(cached_prompt_tokens) / sum(prompt_tokens). Cost is deployment_price (a hop's own cost), so summing over hops of a routed chain does not double-count.

url_options.data: {"sql": "SELECT round(sum(deployment_price), 2) AS \"Spend $\", round(sum(deployment_price) / nullif(count(DISTINCT trace_id), 0), 4) AS \"Dollar per turn\", round(sum(CASE WHEN chat_id <> '' THEN deployment_price END) / nullif(count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN chat_id <> '' THEN chat_id END), 0), 4) AS \"Dollar per conversation\", round(100.0 * sum(CASE WHEN chat_id <> '' THEN deployment_price END) / nullif(sum(deployment_price), 0), 1) AS \"Chat share of spend %\", round(sum(deployment_price) / nullif(sum(total_tokens), 0) * 1000000, 2) AS \"Dollar per Mtok\", round(100.0 * sum(cached_prompt_tokens) / nullif(sum(prompt_tokens), 0), 1) AS \"Prompt cache hit %\" FROM dial_usage_log WHERE request_time >= TIMESTAMP '${__from:date:YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss}' AND request_time < TIMESTAMP '${__to:date:YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss}'"}

panels.title: Cost by outcome
panels.description: Conversations rollup with its own same-grain insight enrichment read as a dotted column (a left join on chat_id) - not a cross-spine join. Cost is the rollup's own total_price, which already sums per-hop costs. Sorted by Dollar per conversation descending, so the worst unit cost is on top. 'unlabelled' is not an outcome: it is the conversations that have no conversation_insights row yet (it can be the large majority), and it dominates every absolute column. A large share of conversations carry no total_price at all (unpriced deployments such as echo / adapters, negligible tokens) and count in the denominator as $0; that share differs by outcome, so read the unit cost as indicative. Rows are conversations whose first_request_time falls in the window, not spend that landed in the window.

url_options.data: {"sql": "SELECT coalesce(to_string(\"conversation_insights.resolution_status\"), 'unlabelled') AS \"Outcome\", count(*) AS \"Conversations\", sum(turn_count) AS \"Turns\", round(sum(turn_count) * 1.0 / count(*), 1) AS \"Turns/conv\", round(sum(total_price), 2) AS \"Cost $\", round(sum(total_price) / count(*), 4) AS \"Dollar per conversation\" FROM conversations WHERE first_request_time >= TIMESTAMP '${__from:date:YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss}' AND first_request_time < TIMESTAMP '${__to:date:YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss}' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 6 DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 200"}

panels.title: Cost by kind of work
panels.description: Conversation cost split by the enriched activity_type / coding_task_type of each chat (conversations spine + conversation_insights read as a dotted column, 30d on first_request_time), sorted by total cost, top 200 groups. '-' is an ASCII hyphen (a non-Latin-1 literal is answered with HTTP 500, so an em dash cannot be used here): it means coding_task_type is unset, which is the norm for non-coding activities and for chats with no insights row at all. 'unlabelled' = no conversation_insights row; it is often the largest bucket (it can be the large majority of conversations and spend), so the labelled breakdown may speak for only a minority of spend. A large share of conversations carry no total_price (unpriced deployments with negligible tokens) and count in the 'Dollar per conversation' denominator as $0 - the same convention as the outcome table above; the unpriced share differs a lot per group, so read the unit cost as indicative.

url_options.data: {"sql": "SELECT coalesce(to_string(\"conversation_insights.activity_type\"), 'unlabelled') AS \"Activity\", coalesce(to_string(\"conversation_insights.coding_task_type\"), '-') AS \"Coding task\", count(*) AS \"Conversations\", sum(turn_count) AS \"Turns\", round(sum(total_price), 2) AS \"Cost $\", round(sum(total_price) / count(*), 4) AS \"Dollar per conversation\" FROM conversations WHERE first_request_time >= TIMESTAMP '${__from:date:YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss}' AND first_request_time < TIMESTAMP '${__to:date:YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss}' GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 5 DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 200"}

panels.title: Cost per turn over time
panels.description: Dollars per turn per UTC day: hop-level `deployment_price` summed and divided by distinct `trace_id` in the same day. Buckets are a fixed 1 day and do not follow panel width, so the first and last points cover a partial day. A fall can mean the same work got cheaper (model mix, caching, routing) OR that cheaper work arrived - read the Turns bars (right axis) before calling it efficiency. Turns with no priced hop count as $0, so the level sits below the cost of priced turns.

url_options.data: {"sql": "SELECT date_bin(1, 'day', request_time) AS ts, sum(deployment_price) / nullif(count(DISTINCT trace_id), 0) AS \"Dollar per turn\", count(DISTINCT trace_id) AS \"Turns\" FROM dial_usage_log WHERE request_time >= TIMESTAMP '${__from:date:YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss}' AND request_time < TIMESTAMP '${__to:date:YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss}' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 LIMIT 1000"}

panels.title: Prompt cache hit rate over time
panels.description: Cached prompt tokens as a share of prompt tokens, in fixed 1-hour buckets (the bucket does not follow the panel width or the time range). Two denominators, because a large share of calls never report a cached-token figure at all - embeddings, toolsets and RAG applications, plus some model deployments on part of their traffic - and those calls can carry a meaningful share of all prompt tokens. 'Cacheable traffic' divides only by the prompt tokens of calls that do report the field; 'all prompt tokens' is the raw share and is diluted by the rest. The third line is the share of each hour's prompt tokens that came from cache-reporting calls: when it dips, a drop in the raw line is missing telemetry, not a caching regression - the raw line can read near zero in an hour where cacheable traffic was almost fully cached. A gap in the rate lines means no call in that hour reported cached tokens; a gap is never 'no traffic'. Efficiency INDICATOR only: ADAS does not record the per-provider cache discount, so no dollar saving can be derived from this. The legend 'mean' is an unweighted mean of hourly rates, not the token-weighted 30-day rate.

url_options.data: {"sql": "SELECT date_bin(1, 'hour', request_time) AS ts, 100.0 * sum(cached_prompt_tokens) / nullif(sum(CASE WHEN cached_prompt_tokens IS NOT NULL THEN prompt_tokens END), 0) AS \"Cache hit % (cacheable traffic)\", 100.0 * sum(cached_prompt_tokens) / nullif(sum(prompt_tokens), 0) AS \"Cache hit % (all prompt tokens)\", 100.0 * coalesce(sum(CASE WHEN cached_prompt_tokens IS NOT NULL THEN prompt_tokens END), 0) / nullif(sum(prompt_tokens), 0) AS \"Cache-reporting share of prompt tokens %\" FROM dial_usage_log WHERE request_time >= TIMESTAMP '${__from:date:YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss}' AND request_time < TIMESTAMP '${__to:date:YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss}' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 LIMIT 1000"}

panels.title: Cost per turn by client type
panels.description: Is an agent turn cheaper or dearer than a chat turn? One row per `usage_client_identity.client_type`, turns counted as distinct `trace_id`, cost as summed `deployment_price` (a hop's own cost, so routed chains are not double-counted); sorted by total cost, dearest first. Cost and token columns are blank where every hop in the bucket is unpriced (e.g. a client type that makes only unpriced calls), and they cover only the priced hops elsewhere — a large share of hops carry no `deployment_price`, so treat the per-turn dollars as a floor. 'unattributed' would hold hops with no identity enrichment row; once the backfill has caught up, that bucket is empty.

url_options.data: {"sql": "SELECT coalesce(\"usage_client_identity.client_type\", 'unattributed') AS \"Client\", count(DISTINCT trace_id) AS \"Turns\", round(sum(deployment_price), 2) AS \"Cost $\", round(sum(deployment_price) / nullif(count(DISTINCT trace_id), 0), 4) AS \"Dollar per turn\", round(sum(total_tokens) * 1.0 / nullif(count(DISTINCT trace_id), 0)) AS \"Tokens per turn\" FROM dial_usage_log WHERE request_time >= TIMESTAMP '${__from:date:YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss}' AND request_time < TIMESTAMP '${__to:date:YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss}' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 3 DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 200"}
